National Parks and Access to the Countryside Act 1949
Protected sites and areas planning review guidance

official_measurement_examples.name: AONB current national dataset
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data reports 34 AONB records from authoritative sources, collector run 24 July 2026; National Landscape is the public-facing rebrand while AONB remains the statutory designation terminology.

official_measurement_examples.name: National park dataset limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data's national-park layer is an administrative-boundary dataset sourced from ONS and is not by itself proof of every statutory planning policy consequence at a parcel.

official_measurement_examples.name: Protected Landscapes duty
official_measurement_examples.fact: The strengthened duty requires relevant authorities to seek to further protected-landscape purposes when exercising affected functions; it is not an automatic development prohibition.

official_measurement_examples.name: Setting matters
official_measurement_examples.fact: Official duty guidance says relevant authorities should consider effects on the setting where functions affect protected landscapes; being outside a mapped boundary does not automatically remove landscape relevance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Designation purpose
official_measurement_examples.fact: AONB designation protects natural beauty under the CROW Act; it does not establish freehold ownership or public access rights.

official_measurement_examples.name: Policy weight
official_measurement_examples.fact: National planning policy gives great weight to conserving and enhancing landscape and scenic beauty in National Parks and National Landscapes, but proposal-specific planning judgment remains necessary.

official_measurement_examples.name: Management plan distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A protected-landscape management plan is important policy evidence but is not a parcel planning permission, title record or development-yield calculation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current policy context
official_measurement_examples.fact: 2026 nature-recovery funding and 30by30 delivery measures do not silently change statutory protected-landscape boundaries or grant/refuse parcel development rights.

core_rules: National Landscape rebrand does not replace statutory AONB terminology
protected-landscape duty is not automatic refusal
administrative national-park geometry is not complete parcel policy evidence
setting effects can matter outside boundary
designation is not public access right
management plan is not planning permission
funding programme does not alter statutory boundary
historic and current designations remain distinct
no parcel protected-landscape clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Planning Data, GOV.UK, Natural England and legislation sources checked 2026-07-26. Current 2026 collector/policy context retained; no parcel promotion.
